newsitem.title: USA: NYSE- June 30-July 3 program trades avg 25.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE- June 30-July 3 program trades avg 25.2 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said Thursday that program trading for the week of June 30 through July 3 amounted to 127.4 million shares a day, or 25.2 percent of the exchanges's average daily volume of 505.1 million shares.
In the previous week, program trading accounted for 20.6 percent of average daily volume, or 108.4 million shares per day.
The exchange said buy programs accounted for for 13.9 percent, and sell programs accounted for 11.3 percent of the average daily volume of program trades.
In all markets, program trading averaged 302 million shares a day during the week, said the NYSE.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, BNP Securities, Natwest, Merrill Lynch, and Salomon Brotheres each executed all or most of their program trading for customers. Morgan Stanley executed most of its program trading for itself.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 71.7 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 26.9 percent of program volume.
Between June 30 and July 3, 13.5 percent of program volume executed by NYSE member firms related to index arbitrage, while another one percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of 41 million or more.
